subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in the system-prompt Runtime line, and what freshness and display contract should it use?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the feature changes model-visible volatile prompt metadata, cache behavior, and agent decision semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
options.body: Add a compact context field using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage, with focused stale, compaction, model-switch, and cache-boundary tests.

options.title: Keep explicit inspection only
options.body: Leave context usage on `/context`, `/status`, `session_status`, and native Codex context tools, then close this feature after maintainers decide passive prompt metadata is not desired.

options.title: Fold into runtime self-context design
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader runtime self-context work and implement the context-usage signal only after that product/API surface is accepted.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
recommendation.body: Add a compact context field using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage, with focused stale, compaction, model-switch, and cache-boundary tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the OpenClaw-owned system prompt Runtime contract, where Peter has the strongest history signal.
